about: Exterior looks of djour's three-star picks, researched from photos (Nov 2026) for js/scene/phl/restaurants.js; build_restaurants.py merges them into data/phl/restaurants.json by name (and hood for Human Robot). address: the street address found in research (looked up on OSM by fetch_eats.py); indoor: no street front of its own.

places.name: a.kitchen
places.notes: Ground floor of the AKA Rittenhouse hotel at 18th & Walnut (135 S 18th St): cream limestone base, run of navy-blue fabric shed awnings over tall dark-framed glass bays, sidewalk cafe tables with boxwood planters. Floor count of the tower is approximate.

places.name: Chengdu
places.notes: Trades as Chengdu Famous Food at 3635-3637 Lancaster Ave. White-painted multi-pane storefront with red-painted end pilasters, long black sign board with the name and a small red logo; window AC units in the upper sash.

places.name: Doro Bet
places.notes: Small Victorian storefront: pale-yellow clapboard bay window with white trim and a bracketed cornice above, tan-brick side wall. Row of dark-green gooseneck barn lamps over the white glass front; square lightbox blade sign with a red/yellow/green chicken logo. Neighbour's 'Diamond Nails' blade sign hangs above.

places.name: Farina di Vita
places.notes: Modern red-brick corner building with a black standing-seam metal box bay cantilevered over the corner entrance (black steel column at the corner). Terracotta clay-tile shed awnings on both faces with bulb string lights under them; copper-framed hanging boards with a white hand logo, and red-circle hand logos on the windows.

places.name: Hiroki
places.notes: Windowless one-storey box of pale board-formed concrete with a huge circular dark-stained timber door (moon gate) and tiny name letters beside it; a dark wood vertical-slat screen rises above the parapet like a second storey. Sits on Front St under the Market-Frankford El, next to a red-brick rowhouse.

places.name: John's Roast Pork
places.notes: Free-standing one-storey shack: rough brick-red stucco walls, a sky-blue fascia band reading the name with 'Established 1930', and a blue canopy over the walk-up order windows with roll-down grilles. Rooftop cut-out pig mascot sign (white pig with red gingham bib) on a pole; red picnic tables outside.

places.name: Machine Shop
places.notes: Inside the Bok Building (1901 S 9th St), a huge buff-brick and limestone Art Deco former school; no own street storefront seen. Model the Bok entrance with its stacked black B-O-K cube sign; the bakery itself shows a yellow MACHINE SHOP board over a counter window inside.

places.name: Midnight & Wicked
places.notes: Actually at 1500 Sansom St (15th & Sansom, Rittenhouse edge, not the Gayborhood); an underground 1920s-style lounge with only a street door. Outside, a black shield-shaped board with gold crest and lettering is mounted on red brick beside white-framed windows, above a barre3 studio sign. Floor count is a guess.

places.name: Parc
places.notes: Parisian bistro at the base of a tall tan-brick tower at 18th & Locust facing Rittenhouse Square: chamfered corner entrance with honey-varnished wooden double doors and tall carved wood panels, slate name board with gooseneck lamps above it, red-framed folding windows under red awnings on both streets, and a sidewalk cafe of wicker bistro chairs. Tower height approximate.

places.name: Royal Izayaka
places.notes: Plain brown-brick building at 2nd & Fulton St with a tan stone stringcourse over the ground floor: two tall glass-block windows flank a cobalt-blue panelled door with a white frame and small-pane transom. The only sign is a red paper lantern with white kanji hanging beside the door; no name sign.

places.name: Scampi
places.notes: Whole storefront painted pastel pink, with an ornate egg-and-dart cornice; recessed green glass door on the left under black letters arched in a curve, a ceiling globe lamp in the recess, and one big window on the right with a white half-height cafe curtain and plants. Wooden bench on the sidewalk; black iron security gate on the neighbouring door.

places.name: Vernick Fish
places.notes: Ground floor of the Comcast Technology Center / Four Seasons tower at 1800 Arch St; only interior shots found, showing floor-to-ceiling glass with dark mullions behind a pale-gray stone base. Sign and door details are inferred, not seen.

places.name: Angelo's Pizzeria
places.notes: Narrow red-brick rowhouse with one long black shed awning spanning the whole front, white script name on its valance; bright red stools/small tables on the sidewalk and a red brick bulkhead under the window.

places.name: Circles + Squares
places.notes: Red-brick corner rowhouse whose ground floor is painted white; a yellow-and-white striped scalloped awning wraps the corner. Square white sign with a black circle-in-square logo; wooden picnic table and teal chairs on the sidewalk.
sources: https://philly.eater.com/ (Pizza Gutt to open as Circles + Squares in permanent location)

places.name: Elixr
places.notes: Symmetric red-brick front: two angled projecting bay windows, each under a small black-and-white striped awning, flank a recessed central black glass door. Pale grey painted bulkhead/base; urn planter by the door. Photo is from Elixr's own site; assumed to be the Sydenham St cafe.

places.name: Fri Sat Sun
places.notes: Bright red brick rowhouse at 261 S 21st with black-framed storefront: golden varnished wooden double doors (No. 261 in gilt on the transom) at left, big window with gilt FRI SAT SUN at right, black-and-white striped awning. In cold months a navy entry vestibule box painted FRIDAY SATURDAY SUNDAY stands in front of the door.

places.name: Human Robot
places.notes: Building photo (listing, ~1 yr old) still shows the former Crime & Punishment Brewing front: red-brick 3-storey Victorian with a two-storey sage-grey pressed-metal bay window over a dark charcoal storefront with multi-pane transoms; a stone Gothic church stands right next door. Human Robot sign wording/colours inferred from their other taprooms (white on black board), not seen at this address.

places.name: Kalaya
places.notes: Tall one-storey former industrial building painted white with a dark forest-green painted brick base band about a quarter of the wall high; a row of tall round-arched multi-pane windows with white muntins and green lower panels. Brass lantern sconces between arches, round gold medallion blade signs, and large potted plants/vines along the wall.
sources: https://www.inquirer.com/ (Kalaya Thai restaurant's new location is 4 times the size, with a bar)

places.name: Mawn
places.notes: Red-brick rowhouse with a dusty slate-blue painted wood storefront and a black shed awning printed 764 in white; round cream blade sign with mawn in brown script at the door side. White globe pendant lights under the awning and a flower box below the big window.

places.name: Mighty Bread
places.notes: Plain red-brick building with black-framed glass double doors lettered in white, a round black blade sign, and a narrow brick side courtyard with small black awnings, cafe tables and plants. Address not given; matched by name only.

places.name: Pietramala
places.notes: Understated: a dark grey shingled pent roof over a wide black-green multi-pane window grid (about 3 rows by 6) on a red brick bulkhead, glass door at left with a small green globe lamp; a bright blue residential door sits to the right. Warm red-orange glow inside at night; no prominent name sign.

places.name: Royal Tavern
places.notes: Ground floor brick painted vivid cobalt blue with white horizontal pinstripes along the top, a single dark-wood-framed window lettered Royal TAVERN in gold, a dark red-brown wooden door at right with a lantern sconce. Upper floors bare red brick; blue blade sign with white letters and a gold lion.

places.name: Smalls Provisions
places.notes: Classic Philly corner store: red-brick rowhouse with an all-black painted wood storefront and bracketed black cornice, angled entrance cut into the corner up a stone step, and a small cream hanging sign reading SMALLS above the corner door.

places.name: Vetri
places.notes: Not a storefront: a Federal-style red-brick townhouse with a white marble arched doorway and fanlight over a varnished wood door (small brass oval plaque), white marble steps, and two tall 6-over-6 windows with rust-brown wooden shutters and gooseneck lamps; dense potted plants crowd the front.

places.name: Backyard Cravings
places.notes: New shop (opened Oct 2026) at 1429 Wolf St, South Philly, in a row of red-brick rowhouses: white-painted facade with bright green pilasters, cornice and door, and two small green-and-white striped awnings over the windows either side of the door. The board in the opening photo reads 'Bottega Creations' with a round green 'BC' logo on the door glass (same BC initials); sign wording is uncertain.

places.name: DiNic's
places.notes: Not a street storefront: an indoor counter stall inside Reading Terminal Market (1136 Arch St) with red counter stools and stainless/wood-plank counter. Signature is a big round sign: cream/yellow centre with red 'ROAST PORK AND BEEF' and a pig, ringed in red reading 'TOMMY DINIC'S SINCE 1954', plus a long wooden 'TOMMY DINIC'S' signboard and a red neon accent.

places.name: Emily Wilson Pastry
places.notes: No retail storefront: Em Wilson is a micro-bakery working from a production kitchen at 4500 Worth St Unit A206 (the Globe Dye Works mill complex, Frankford/Bridesburg edge), selling by pre-order, pop-ups and markets. Model as a 19th-century red-brick mill with rows of multi-pane industrial windows and no signage; no photo of the bakery's own frontage exists.

places.name: Her Place Supper Club
places.notes: 1740 Sansom St: tiny ground floor faced in dark brown brick (#5a3b30) with one wide black-framed window (half café curtain) on the left and a black door up a few stone steps on the right; flower window box under the window, three small pink-red gooseneck lamps above, and a small purple neon 'her place' script in the window. The neighbouring wall to the left carries a black-and-white line-drawing mural.

places.name: Human Robot
places.notes: Kensington/Fishtown taproom at 1710 N 5th St (the only non-Brewerytown Philly-north location found): old red-brick industrial building with arched-top windows, a tall vertical black blade sign spelling HUMAN ROBOT in white, a black fascia board over a glass entry, and a metal roll-up shutter covered in colourful graffiti art. Inside, a glowing dachshund 'HUMAN ROBOT' sign is the brand mark.

places.name: Liberty Kitchen
places.notes: 1400 N Front St, directly under the elevated Market-Frankford El tracks (green steel columns): a plain cream-white painted brick corner box with black multi-pane windows, black gooseneck lamps, small blue window boxes, and a navy rectangular board 'LIBERTY KITCHEN / DELI · MARKET · CAFE' in white mounted on the wall near the corner.

places.name: Middle Child
places.notes: Red-brick rowhouse with white-trimmed sash windows above; the ground floor has a wide off-white fascia band with big green block letters MIDDLE CHILD, black gooseneck lamps over it, and black-framed multi-pane glass below. Green metal bistro chairs/tables and a bench on the sidewalk.

places.name: Ogawa
places.notes: Ogawa Sushi & Kappo at 310 Market St: a black storefront in an Old City brick commercial block, with a black shed awning whose face carries a big red circle (ensō-style) and white brush-script 'Ogawa'. Dark glass and a recessed glass door; minimalist.

places.name: Porco's Porchetteria
places.notes: Shares a low one-storey building with Small Oven Pastry Shop at 2204 Washington Ave. Whole exterior is painted as a mural: sky-blue walls with bold white diagonal stripes, white script 'Small Oven', red script 'Porco's' with a red arrow and 'ORDER' pointing at a small walk-up counter window, plus a dark roll-up gate.

places.name: Sakana
places.notes: Sakana Omakase at 616 S 2nd St (Queen Village/Society Hill edge): red-brick rowhouse whose ground floor is clad in smooth white/cream stucco-stone with an arched dark wood door and a large window; a white box sign with red 'SAKANA' lettering projects above the entry.

places.name: Suraya
places.notes: Wide, charcoal-grey painted brick building with black steel industrial multi-pane windows upstairs; a huge white flowing script 'Suraya' spans the facade above the ground floor, which is a row of red-framed multi-pane glass doors/windows. Red bistro chairs and greenery out front.

places.name: Zahav
places.notes: Low, single-storey dark chocolate-brown brick pavilion at the foot of the Society Hill Towers (a concrete high-rise looms behind). Big brushed-aluminium lowercase 'zahav' letters on the blank brick parapet above a band of dark-framed glass; entry up a short flight of steps under a navy shed awning; lots of ivy and trees around, plus a small patio.

places.name: Caphe Roasters
places.notes: Converted red-brick mill building (J-Centrel) with tall black steel multi-pane industrial windows; a wide black sign band with white serif lettering spans over black-framed glass doors. Courtyard patio with tables beside it.

places.name: Dolores 2nd St
places.notes: Corner-deli rowhouse at 1841 S 2nd St: red brick with white upper window frames; a dark red board with cream script 'Dolores' sits on a black flat canopy over a cream storefront with red-framed door and window. Only a partial (older) selfie photo seen.

places.name: Emmett
places.notes: Clipped-corner entrance at 161 W Girard: whole ground floor painted deep navy with a heavy cornice, white script '161' on the corner fascia, a green glowing 'emmett' script sign in the transom over silver double glass doors, and window boxes of greenery on tan sills. Cream painted brick above.

places.name: High Street
places.notes: Ground floor of the limestone Franklin Building at 101 S 9th St (9th and Chestnut): a row of black shed awnings with spaced white 'HIGH STREET' lettering over black-framed plate glass, with ornate green-glass lanterns on brackets between bays.

places.name: JG Skyhigh
places.notes: Bar is on the 60th floor of the Comcast Technology Center (Four Seasons, 19th and Arch); at street level it is the tower's tall glass atrium base screened by vertical grey metal fins, with no storefront signage of its own.

places.name: Lil Nick's
places.notes: Corner deli at 1311 W Moyamensing Ave: red-brick rowhouse with a white-sided bay above, maroon shed awnings wrapping both street faces with white lettering ('Lil' Nick's', 'We Deliver'), a white projecting board sign, and a café table with a blue umbrella out front.

places.name: Middle Child Clubhouse
places.notes: Ground floor of a red-brick apartment building on N Front St: a deep green fascia with white serif 'Middle Child' over green steel multi-pane window walls between white-painted brick piers, a green glass entry vestibule, and a green neon 'CLUBHOUSE' sign glowing inside.

places.name: Paesano's
places.notes: Recessed entry with varnished warm-wood window frames, black tile bulkhead and a black-and-white checkerboard tile vestibule floor, under the Italian Market's metal stall canopy on 9th St; a cream board with dark lettering and a red window banner carry the name.

places.name: ReAnimator
places.notes: Narrow wedge-shaped red-brick corner building; the short end holds a single tall black-framed glass door flanked by two small sconces, with a pale grey board sign above it. Small café tables and potted plants line the side sidewalk.

places.name: Sang Kee
places.notes: Red-brick building with a curved tan bamboo/thatch-style awning over dark-tinted plate glass, a dark green fascia band, and a white projecting sign with green lettering, red Chinese characters and a duck logo. Green awnings continue around the side street.

places.name: Trattoria @ Heavy Metal Sausage

signs.text: HEAVY METAL SPECIALTY MEATS SAUSAGE CO.

places.notes: Rowhouse butcher shop at 1527 W Porter St (the trattoria is its BYOB dinner): black-painted storefront with a large black multi-pane window over a red-brick bulkhead, a dark shingled pent roof above, white window lettering, and a green glass globe lamp by the door.
